Exam mechanics research: the item count and passing-score threshold for the Class D knowledge test are NOT published anywhere by NDDOT that could be found after genuine effort -- checked the full manual text, the manual's landing page, the Driver License Requirements FAQ page (dot.nd.gov/driver/driver-education/driver-license-requirements), the Online Services for Drivers page, an NDDOT site search, and North Dakota Century Code Chapter 39-06 (the driver's license statute); none state a question count or passing percentage, so both are left UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed. One mechanic WAS confirmed from an official-adjacent source: nd.knowtodrive.com (linked directly by both the printed manual and dot.nd.gov as where applicants 'may take your knowledge test immediately') redirects to knowtodrive.com/northdakota, the state's own contracted online testing vendor; its FAQ page states verbatim 'There is a 60-minute time limit to complete the test' for the Class D Knowledge Test, and that each test attempt costs $10.00 -- so the North Dakota Class D knowledge test IS CONFIRMED TIMED at 60 minutes, but question count and passing score remain unconfirmed. Content-depth rationale: this is NDDOT's real, current 47-page manual (2,608 lines of extracted text) covering licensing/permits/GDL rules for 14-17 year olds (with a 50-hour supervised-driving log and parent-coaching/teen-risk-statistics section), signs/signals/pavement markings, right-of-way/roundabouts/interstate driving, speed limits/passing/following distance, vehicle equipment/registration/insurance/parking/towing/crash reporting, DUI and drug law with the state's specific suspension-day and point-system tables, seat belts/child restraints/heatstroke, winter driving/skids/flooding/distracted driving, sharing the road with trucks/motorcycles/bicycles/pedestrians, and a full recreational-vehicles section (motorized bicycles, off-highway vehicles, snowmobiles) with their own numeric rules. This genuinely and honestly supports a bank of roughly 250-270 distinct, non-repetitive, grounded questions -- shorter than some other states' 100+ page manuals, so the pool lands toward the lower-middle of the site's usual 250-300 target rather than the top of it; no filler, invented facts, or restated questions were added to pad the count. Price matches this project's fixed Driver-track rate ($4.99) site-wide. Every question is grounded in a specific cited passage of the fetched official manual text, or (for the 60-minute time limit and $10 test fee) the state's own designated online-testing vendor FAQ; none are invented or generic 'common knowledge' items.
